newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police round up Mafiosi in dawn swoops.
newsitem.headline: Italian police round up Mafiosi in dawn swoops.

text.p: Police said on Saturday they had arrested more than 50 alleged mobsters in dawn swoops across southern Italy.

Police in the southeastern port city of Taranto said they had arrested some 40 suspected members of a powerful clan on charges of murder, trafficking of drugs and counterfeit money, and extortion. Some 400 police agents took place in the raid.

In the eastern Sicilian town of Paterno, near Catania, 15 alleged mobsters of the "Santa Barbara" clan were rounded up in a dawn swoop. They face charges of murder, criminal association and sexual assault, police said.

In Palermo, eight jailed Mafiosi were informed that they were being investigated in connection with several murders in the Sicilian capital during the 1980s, including that of former Palermo soccer club owner Roberto Parisi and Republican Party senator Ignazio Mineo.
The investigation was based in part on the testimony of turncoat Emanuele Di Filippo, who took part in some of the murders himself, police said.
